content.comment_body: Hello, I'm new here and would appreciate feedback on MODBUS connectivity between [product_name] modules (currently considering [product_name] 24CEo). The system consists of one PC, a central controller, and 11 remote controllers over 2.2 km. Given the distance, I was considering using several RS485 extenders (about every kilometer or less) and connecting everything using MODBUS. Is this feasible, and what challenges might arise? Thanks in advance.

Unless [product_name] is notably different from the standard, it utilizes Modbus TCP/IP (ethernet) instead of RTU. Using fiber optics might be your best choice; it would simplify the setup compared to employing extenders.

The [product_name] variant has Ethernet functionality equivalent to the standard version. However, to use Modbus TCP/IP, it must be an FS4 model ([version_no], second generation or newer). Previous generations, like the first [version_no], can only use Ethernet TCP/IP and not Modbus TCP/IP.

Sharing my experience: for devices requiring MODBUS RTU, I use affordable MODBUS TCP-to-RTU converters (e.g., Protoss PE11). It's essential to have a separate converter for each device, as polling multiple devices through one converter may cause communication issues—if a device does not respond, the subsequent addresses might not be polled. For instance, with devices at addresses 2, 3, 4, and 5 in the network, if address 3 fails to reply, devices 4 and 5 won't be polled since they appear as a single device with one IP address. So, using one converter per device solves this problem, and fortunately, these converters are not costly.

analysis.insight_summary: The thread discusses technical challenges and practical considerations when connecting multiple [product_name] controllers and a PC across 2.2 km using MODBUS. The main topics include compatibility with MODBUS TCP/IP rather than RTU, preferred networking methods (such as fiber optics), hardware requirements, and concerns about scalability—especially when using TCP-to-RTU converters where device polling can fail if a single device is unresponsive.
